message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates).
• “No‑limit” highways (e.g., I‑10, I‑35) have no posted maximum, but drivers must still obey “reasonable and prudent” speed. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Seat Belt & Child Restraint** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | Texas Transportation Code §545.002 | | **DUI / Driving Under Influence** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02%).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §§545.021–545.023 | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Texas Transportation Code §545.025 | | **Headlights & Signal Use** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Turn signals must be used at least 100 ft before turning. | Texas Transportation Code §545.030 | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • Stop at stop signs; yield at yield signs.
• At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has priority unless otherwise indicated. | Texas Transportation Code §545.040 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• No passing on either side of a stopped bus with flashing red lights. | Texas Transportation Code §545.050 | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep to the right lane unless passing.
• Do not drive in the left lane on freeways unless overtaking. | Texas Transportation Code §545.060 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in fire lanes, handicap spaces (unless you have a permit), or on sidewalks.
• Parking meters and municipal regulations apply in cities. | Texas Transportation Code §545.070 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Vehicles must be registered annually.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection (except in some counties). | Texas Transportation Code §545.080 | | **Toll Roads & Bridges** | • Texas has several toll roads (e.g., TXDOT’s toll lanes, toll bridges).
• Toll payment methods include electronic toll tags (e.g., TxTag). | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) | | **Emergency Vehicle Rules** | • Drivers must pull over to the right and stop when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches. | Texas Transportation Code §545.090 | | **Driving While Unlicensed** | • Operating a vehicle without a valid Texas driver’s license is a misdemeanor. | Texas Transportation Code §545.011 | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The primary legal source for all traffic laws. *Website:* https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TX/htm/TX.545.htm 2. **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** – Provides driver’s handbook, licensing info, and updates on law changes. *Website:* https://www.txdmv.gov/ 3. **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Offers information on road conditions, tolls, and infrastructure projects. *Website:* https://www.txdot.gov/ 4. **Local County & City Ordinances** – Some municipalities have additional parking, speed, or noise ordinances. Check your city’s official website. 5. **Legal Resources** – For specific legal questions or recent case law, consult the Texas Courts’ website or a licensed attorney. --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s a legal requirement and saves lives. - **Avoid distractions** – hands‑free only. - **Know your speed limit** – especially on rural highways where limits can be higher. - **Respect school buses** – they’re a priority for child safety. - **Stay alert for toll lanes** – they often have different rules and enforcement. Feel free to let me know if you need deeper details on any specific area (e.g., DUI penalties, toll payment options, or how to register a vehicle).
